## Definitions

- [statement] Parkin is an E3 ligase that functions together with the ubiquitin kinase PINK1 to flag damaged mitochondria for removal via a selective form of autophagy known as mitophagy. (high confidence) — https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ady0240 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24896179/
- [statement] Mutations in the Parkin and PINK1 proteins are the most common form of autosomal recessive PD. (high confidence) — https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ady0240 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789816/
- [statement] pS65-Ubiquitin (pUb) is a PINK1 substrate, and a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant page says the differential effectiveness of PINK1 activator compounds will be determined by analyzing specific biomarkers. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11100876/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/grant/pink1-activators-treating-parkinsons-disease

## Structure and components

- [statement] The buntanetap Phase 3 study in early PD did not meet its primary endpoint of MDS-UPDRS Part II, according to the published paper and Alzforum. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s44400-026-00148-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/buntanetap

## How it works

- [statement] Alzforum states the company did not report on the primary endpoint in the group as a whole when it announced results on July 2, 2024; Fierce Biotech says the release skirted the question of whether buntanetap moved the needle on the main goal. - [statement] In the phase 1b study of anle138b in PD (NCT04685265), the conference abstract reports 70 participants were enrolled in cohorts A-E and that anle138b was safe and well tolerated when administered 7-28 days; the registry lists 70 actual participants. (medium confidence) — https://www.mdsabstracts.org/abstract/anle138b-p1-02-a-randomised-double-blinded-placebo-controlled-phase-1b-study-to-investigate-safety-tolerability-pharmacokinetics-and-pharmacodynamics-of-the-oligomer-modulator-anle138b-in-parkins/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04685265
- [statement] Ahlskog and Uitti argue that interpretation of the ADAGIO rasagiline delayed-start trials is problematic because of divergent results with the 2 symptomatically beneficial doses and variability in UPDRS scores with active rasagiline that was twice the magnitude of the major finding. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2865777/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Mission states that its MTX325-101 Phase 1b study is designed to establish clinical proof-of-mechanism using a wide range of biomarkers and imaging measures, and the registry's official title for NCT07630545 includes assessing CNS penetration, biodistribution, and biomarkers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://missiontherapeutics.com/mission-therapeutics-doses-first-parkinsons-patient-in-phase-1b-study-of-potential-disease-modifying-treatment-mtx325/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30 · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07630545

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The buntanetap Phase 3 study in early PD (registry NCT05357989) enrolled 523 participants in a 6-month, randomized, double-blind, dose-ranging design testing 10 mg and 20 mg buntanetap against placebo. - [statement] A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1a trial of anle138b in healthy volunteers enrolled 68 participants and reported exposure levels above the fully effective exposure in the MI2 mouse Parkinson model at multiple doses of 200 mg. - [statement] PADOVA is a Phase 2b, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study in which individuals with early-stage PD on stable symptomatic monotherapy (levodopa or MAO-Bi) receive intravenous prasinezumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39798255/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines · also: https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2024-12-19

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] UCB announced on 16 December 2024 that ORCHESTRA, a study of minzasolmin, an oral small-molecule alpha-synuclein misfolding inhibitor, did not meet its primary and secondary clinical endpoints in early Parkinson’s disease. (high confidence) — https://www.ucb.com/newsroom/press-releases/article/findings-from-minzasolmin-proof-of-concept-orchestra-study-shape-next-steps-in-ucb-parkinson-s-research-program · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/minzasolmin
- [statement] The Lancet's Department of Error notice states that the appendix of the PADOVA article has been corrected as of July 2, 2026. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-02) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140673626013012 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines
- [statement] Recent reviews state that no disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease has been established: one says there are currently no disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), and a trial-pipeline analysis says there are still no treatments to modify the course of the disease. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-17) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01483-9 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13442941/
- [statement] A ClinicalTrials.gov-based analysis of Parkinson's disease drug trials registered between 2015–2024 reports 444 trials, of which 42% were in Phase 1, 46% in Phase 2 and 12% in Phase 3, with 63% evaluating symptomatic therapies and 37% testing disease-modifying therapies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13442941/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Mari and Mestre describe a “valley of death” in Parkinson's disease modification populated by failures such as the various NET-PD trials, the ADAGIO trial, the more recent α-Synuclein immunotherapy trials and the Ven-glustat trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8920063/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Isradipine evidence is split: the STEADY-PD III report concluded that isradipine did not slow clinical progression, while a re-analysis of STEADY-PD II data reports significantly smaller total and part 3 UPDRS scores with 10 mg/day ER isradipine than placebo at trial end, with post hoc adjustment for symptomatic therapy diminishing the statistical significance. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8922308/
- [statement] In FAIRPARK-II (NCT02655315), a phase 2 trial in participants with newly diagnosed Parkinson's disease who had never received levodopa, the authors report that the mean MDS-UPDRS total score worsened by 15.6 points with deferiprone and 6.3 points with placebo (difference, 9.3 points; 95% confidence interval, 6.3 to 12.2; P<0.001) at 36 weeks, and the trial team's statement likewise reports greater deterioration with deferiprone than with placebo. (high confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2209254 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/FAIRPARK-II-Statement-from-the-clinical-trial-team.pdf
- [statement] The FAIRPARK-II trial team's statement says that 4 other independent deferiprone trials involving about 240 people with Parkinson's disease, in which all participants were already receiving dopamine replacement drugs, observed no worsening of symptoms, and that this difference is probably where the explanation for the conflicting results lies. (low confidence) — https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/FAIRPARK-II-Statement-from-the-clinical-trial-team.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Reviewers report that disease-modification trials in neurodegenerative disorders have struggled to separate symptomatic effects of putative agents from disease modification, and that documenting a disease-modifying effect is difficult for a Parkinson's disease drug with symptomatic benefit. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2865777/
- [statement] A systematic review that searched 1980–2015 included 128 RCTs (84 in AD, 44 in PD) and concluded that none of the included studies convincingly demonstrated disease-modification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] A PRISMA-compliant review of phase II and III disease-modifying trials (2020-2025) with at least one target-engagement biomarker included 26 trials (PD=19, MSA=4, DLB=3); the authors report that only 8/26 studies demonstrated both target engagement and statistically significant clinical benefit and that nine trials showed target engagement without clinical benefit. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42861702/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Authors of two reviews attribute the lack of success of disease-modification trials to factors including the complexity of Parkinson's disease, variability between patients and biomarkers for stratification, advanced pathology at diagnosis, insensitive clinical endpoints and scales, and intervention timing in advanced stages of neurodegeneration. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01483-9 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13435201/
- [statement] In the open-label noncontrolled Mullin trial, scores on part 3 of the Movement Disorders Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale decreased (ie, improved) by 6.8 points. - [statement] In a 52-week phase 2 randomised trial of ambroxol in Parkinson disease dementia, 55 patients were randomised and the authors report no evidence to suggest differences between groups on primary or secondary outcomes. ## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] ORCHESTRA (NCT04658186) was a Phase 2a, randomised, placebo-controlled, 18-month study of oral minzasolmin at 180mg/day or 360mg/day versus placebo in early-stage Parkinson’s disease, with primary endpoint progression in the MDS-UPDRS Parts I–III sum score. (high confidence) — https://www.ucb.com/newsroom/press-releases/article/findings-from-minzasolmin-proof-of-concept-orchestra-study-shape-next-steps-in-ucb-parkinson-s-research-program · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/minzasolmin
- [statement] In PADOVA, the primary endpoint of time to confirmed motor progression was not met: Roche reports HR=0.84 and p=0.0657, and the Lancet paper reports a non-significant delay in motor progression with prasinezumab versus placebo. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-30) — https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2024-12-19 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673626008652
- [statement] SURE-PD3 (NCT02642393), a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of inosine in early Parkinson's disease, randomized 298 participants and closed early after a prespecified interim futility analysis; the authors report MDS-UPDRS progression of 11.1 points per year with inosine versus 9.9 with placebo (P = .18). (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34519802/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02642393
- [statement] STEADY-PD III (NCT02168842), a phase 3 trial that randomized 336 patients with early Parkinson's disease to isradipine 5 mg twice daily or placebo for 36 months, reported adjusted least-squares mean changes in total UPDRS of 2.99 versus 3.26 points (treatment effect —0.27; P = 0.85), and its authors conclude that isradipine did not slow clinical progression. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02168842
- [statement] In the SPARK phase 2 trial (NCT03318523) of cinpanemab in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report the trial was stopped after the week 72 interim analysis owing to lack of efficacy, with a week 52 change in MDS-UPDRS of 10.8 points in the control group versus 10.5, 11.3 and 10.9 points in the 250-mg, 1250-mg and 3500-mg groups. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35921450/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-two-study-outcomes-disappoint-parkinsons-pipeline-remains-strong
- [statement] MOVES-PD, which evaluated the glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat, was described as unsuccessful in a Movement Disorders review, and its authors report that venglustat showed no beneficial treatment effect compared with placebo. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37479372/
- [statement] MJFF states that trials of other drugs in the same class, including NLY01 and PT320, reported no meaningful effect, and MedPage Today reports that the pegylated exenatide analogue NLY01 found no overall benefit compared with placebo but suggested benefits in younger patients. (low confidence) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.medpagetoday.com/neurology/parkinsonsdisease/114113
- [statement] NeurologyLive reports that treatment-emergent adverse events led to study drug withdrawal in 11.2% of BIIB122/DNL151-treated LUMA participants versus 4.6% of placebo-treated participants. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://www.neurologylive.com/view/lrrk2-inhibitor-biib122-fails-slow-early-stage-parkinson-disease · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
- [statement] LIGHTHOUSE (NCT05418673), a Phase 3 study of BIIB122/DNL151 in participants with Parkinson's disease and pathogenic LRRK2 variants, is registered as TERMINATED with the reason Sponsor Decision and 7 actual participants; NeurologyLive attributes the June 2023 termination to complexity and a projected completion date of 2031 rather than any safety or efficacy concern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT05418673 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense · also: https://www.neurologylive.com/view/lrrk2-inhibitor-biib122-fails-slow-early-stage-parkinson-disease
- [statement] A news report on a conference presentation says selnoflast motor outcomes were exploratory: MDS-UPDRS Part III improved by two to three points in the selnoflast group versus worsening by a point or less on placebo, and average differences were small and not statistically significant. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-27) — https://www.alzforum.org/news/conference-coverage/nlrp3-inhibitor-passes-muster-early-parkinsons-trial · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets
- [statement] A review reports that in sargramostim, a recombinant GMCSF, undergoing extended phase 1 testing, initial results with 8 weeks of treatment in 20 patients with PD showed increased numbers and suppressive function of peripheral T regulatory cells and a modest reduction in UPDRS part III scores versus the placebo arm. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11492043/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Buntanetap, formerly Posiphen, is described as a small molecule that inhibits translation of aggregation-prone proteins including APP, tau and α-synuclein; Alzforum notes Posiphen reportedly blocks translation of α-synuclein mRNA. (high confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s44400-026-00148-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/buntanetap
- [statement] The paper reports that buntanetap improved cognition in a post-hoc analysis, with nominally statistically significant dose-dependent benefits in amyloid-positive PD patients with mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia; Alzforum notes MMSE was not listed as a study outcome. (high confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s44400-026-00148-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/buntanetap
- [statement] Two sources give different sizes for the buntanetap subgroup with MMSE scores of 20 to 28: Alzforum reports 173 patients and the paper reports 182 participants. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/buntanetap · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44400-026-00148-x
- [statement] UCB states it has initiated measures to terminate the extension phase of the minzasolmin program, and Alzforum and the Michael J. Fox Foundation state that the companies terminated the long-term extension or do not plan to continue testing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.ucb.com/newsroom/press-releases/article/findings-from-minzasolmin-proof-of-concept-orchestra-study-shape-next-steps-in-ucb-parkinson-s-research-program · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/minzasolmin, https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-mixed-results-two-experimental-drugs-targeting-alpha-synuclein
- [statement] The Michael J. Fox Foundation interview states the ORCHESTRA trial was launched before the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay existed, so it is not known for sure that enrolled participants had the misfolded alpha-synuclein pathology the drug targeted. (low confidence) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-mixed-results-two-experimental-drugs-targeting-alpha-synuclein · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
- [statement] The primary outcomes registered for the anle138b phase 1b study (NCT04685265) are safety measures such as incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and the conference abstract states efficacy trials in patients with synucleinopathies are planned. (medium confidence) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04685265 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap · also: https://www.mdsabstracts.org/abstract/anle138b-p1-02-a-randomised-double-blinded-placebo-controlled-phase-1b-study-to-investigate-safety-tolerability-pharmacokinetics-and-pharmacodynamics-of-the-oligomer-modulator-anle138b-in-parkins/
- [statement] The Lancet PADOVA paper describes prasinezumab as a humanised monoclonal antibody that binds the C-terminus of aggregated forms of α-synuclein. (medium confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673626008652 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines · also: https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2024-12-19
- [statement] The Lancet paper's interpretation states that although PADOVA did not meet the primary endpoint, prespecified exploratory evidence suggests clinical activity of prasinezumab, supporting continued investigation in the phase 3 PARAISO trial (NCT07174310). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-30) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673626008652 · keywords: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials, Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07174310
- [statement] Roche announced its decision to proceed with Phase III development of prasinezumab, and a Michael J. Fox Foundation news page described the drug as moving into the Phase III stage of clinical trials.
